classification.difficultyReason: Reframe the target average speed as a total time allowance, recognise that the first leg already consumes it, and explain why any remaining travel makes the target impossible.

content.prompt:
Shari travels at 50 km/h for 10 km. For the next 10 km she wants to drive fast enough to make her average speed 100 km/h over the 20 km trip.

Advise Shari about reaching this average speed.

answer.short: For 100 km/h over 20 km, she must complete the whole journey in 12 minutes. She has already spent 12 minutes to travel 10 km at 50 km/h, so it is impossible.
answer.worked:
Required time for the whole journey:
$$\begin{align*}t_{\text{total}}&=\frac{d_{\text{total}}}{s_{\text{average}}}\\t_{\text{total}}&=\frac{20}{100}\\t_{\text{total}}&=0.2\text{ h}\\t_{\text{total}}&=12\text{ min}\end{align*}$$
Time already spent:
$$\begin{align*}t_{\text{first}}&=\frac{d_{\text{first}}}{s_{\text{first}}}\\t_{\text{first}}&=\frac{10}{50}\\t_{\text{first}}&=0.2\text{ h}\\t_{\text{first}}&=12\text{ min}\end{align*}$$
She has already used all 12 minutes allowed for the whole journey. The remaining 10 km takes additional time at any finite speed, so an average speed of 100 km/h is impossible.
